title: Outer loadings and indicator reliability
summary: An outer loading is the correlation between an indicator and its construct; its square, the indicator reliability, tells how much of the item the construct explains.

body.text: For a reflective construct the [[outer-loading]] of an indicator is its correlation with the construct score. Its square is the [[indicator-reliability]]: the share of the indicator's variance explained by the construct.

body.explanation: λᵢ is the standardised outer loading of indicator i. A loading of .708 gives λ² ≈ .50: the construct explains half of the item's variance.

body.text: Hair et al. (2022) recommend loadings of about .708 or more; items between .40 and .70 should be removed only if that raises composite reliability or AVE above their thresholds and the content of the construct survives; items below .40 are candidates for removal. These are heuristics, not tests.

[[outer-weight]]s show each indicator's contribution to the composite score. For reflective constructs they are rarely interpreted; for composites they are the main result. Note also that classic PLS loadings tend to overstate the loadings of a common factor: in the TAM example peou4 loads .784 under PLS and .644 under PLSc.

mistake.title: Deleting every item below .708 automatically
mistake.text: Mechanical deletion can narrow a construct until it no longer covers its definition, and it capitalises on sample idiosyncrasies. Look at content, at the effect on reliability and AVE, and report every deletion.

tryIt.task: Run the TAM example and read the outer loadings. Square the lowest one: how much of that item does its construct explain?

checks.question: An indicator loads .65 on its construct. What is its indicator reliability?

options.feedback: The loading is a correlation; reliability is its square.
That is the square root of .65, the wrong direction.

checks.question: An item loads .65, its construct has ρC = .88 and AVE = .58, and the item covers an aspect no other item covers. What do the guidelines suggest?

options.text: Keep it: reliability and AVE are already adequate and removing it would narrow the content.
options.feedback: Correct. Removal of .40–.70 items is only considered if it is needed to reach the thresholds and content permits.

options.text: Delete it because it is below .708.
options.feedback: .708 is a heuristic for good indicators, not a deletion rule.

options.text: Make the construct formative so the loading does not matter.
options.feedback: The measurement model follows from theory, not from one item's loading.
